saetze.text: “Look at dat Buck.

saetze.text: François was obdurate, but when he turned his back Buck again displaced Sol-leks, who was not at all unwilling to go.

saetze.text: “Now, by Gar, I feex you!”

saetze.text: Buck remembered the man in the red sweater, and retreated slowly; nor did he attempt to charge in when Sol-leks was once more brought forward.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: But he circled just beyond the range of the club, snarling with bitterness and rage; and while he circled he watched the club so as to dodge it if thrown by François, for he was become wise in the way of clubs.

saetze.text: François followed him up, whereupon he again retreated.

saetze.text: After some time of this, François threw down the club, thinking that Buck feared a thrashing.

saetze.text: But Buck was in open revolt.

saetze.text: He wanted, not to escape a clubbing, but to have the leadership.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: It was his by right.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: He had earned it, and he would not be content with less.

saetze.text: Between them they ran him about for the better part of an hour.

saetze.text: He dodged.

saetze.text: They cursed him, and his fathers and mothers before him, and all his seed to come after him down to the remotest generation, and every hair on his body and drop of blood in his veins; and he answered curse with snarl and kept out of their reach.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: He did not try to run away, but retreated around and around the camp, advertising plainly that when his desire was met, he would come in and be good.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership

saetze.text: François sat down and scratched his head.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Perrault looked at his watch and swore.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Time was flying, and they should have been on the trail an hour gone.

saetze.text: François scratched his head again.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: He shook it and grinned sheepishly at the courier, who shrugged his shoulders in sign that they were beaten.

saetze.text: Then François went up to where Sol-leks stood and called to Buck.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Buck laughed, as dogs laugh, yet kept his distance.

saetze.text: François unfastened Sol-leks’s traces and put him back in his old place.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: The team stood harnessed to the sled in an unbroken line, ready for the trail.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: There was no place for Buck save at the front.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Once more François called, and once more Buck laughed and kept away.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: “T’row down de club,”

saetze.text: Perrault commanded.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: François complied, whereupon Buck trotted in, laughing triumphantly, and swung around into position at the head of the team.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: His traces were fastened, the sled broken out, and with both men running they dashed out on to the river trail.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Highly as the dog-driver had forevalued Buck, with his two devils, he found, while the day was yet young, that he had undervalued.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: At a bound Buck took up the duties of leadership; and where judgment was required, and quick thinking and quick acting, he showed himself the superior even of Spitz, of whom François had never seen an equal.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: But it was in giving the law and making his mates live up to it, that Buck excelled.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Dave and Sol-leks did not mind the change in leadership.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: It was none of their business.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Their business was to toil, and toil mightily, in the traces.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: So long as that were not interfered with, they did not care what happened.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Billee, the good-natured, could lead for all they cared, so long as he kept order.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: The rest of the team, however, had grown unruly during the last days of Spitz, and their surprise was great now that Buck proceeded to lick them into shape.

saetze.text: Pike, who pulled at Buck’s heels, and who never put an ounce more of his weight against the breast-band than he was compelled to do, was swiftly and repeatedly shaken for loafing; and ere the first day was done he was pulling more than ever before in his life.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: The first night in camp, Joe, the sour one, was punished roundly—a thing that Spitz had never succeeded in doing.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Buck simply smothered him by virtue of superior weight, and cut him up till he ceased snapping and began to whine for mercy.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: The general tone of the team picked up immediately.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: It recovered its old-time solidarity, and once more the dogs leaped as one dog in the traces.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: At the Rink Rapids two native huskies, Teek and Koona, were added; and the celerity with which Buck broke them in took away François’s breath.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: “No, nevaire!

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Heem worth one t’ousan’ dollair, by Gar!

saetze.text: Eh?

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: He was ahead of the record then, and gaining day by day.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: The trail was in excellent condition, well packed and hard, and there was no new-fallen snow with which to contend.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: It was not too cold.

saetze.text: The temperature dropped to fifty below zero and remained there the whole trip.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: The men rode and ran by turn, and the dogs were kept on the jump, with but infrequent stoppages.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: The Thirty Mile River was comparatively coated with ice, and they covered in one day going out what had taken them ten days coming in.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: In one run they made a sixty-mile dash from the foot of Lake Le Barge to the White Horse Rapids.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Across Marsh, Tagish, and Bennett (seventy miles of lakes), they flew so fast that the man whose turn it was to run towed behind the sled at the end of a rope.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: And on the last night of the second week they topped White Pass and dropped down the sea slope with the lights of Skaguay and of the shipping at their feet.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: It was a record run.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Each day for fourteen days they had averaged forty miles.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: For three days Perrault and François threw chests up and down the main street of Skaguay and were deluged with invitations to drink, while the team was the constant centre of a worshipful crowd of dog-busters and mushers.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Then three or four western bad men aspired to clean out the town, were riddled like pepper-boxes for their pains, and public interest turned to other idols.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Next came official orders.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: François called Buck to him, threw his arms around him, wept over him.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: And that was the last of François and Perrault.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Like other men, they passed out of Buck’s life for good.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: A Scotch half-breed took charge of him and his mates, and in company with a dozen other dog-teams he started back over the weary trail to Dawson.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: It was no light running now, nor record time, but heavy toil each day, with a heavy load behind; for this was the mail train, carrying word from the world to the men who sought gold under the shadow of the Pole.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Buck did not like it, but he bore up well to the work, taking pride in it after the manner of Dave and Sol-leks, and seeing that his mates, whether they prided in it or not, did their fair share.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: It was a monotonous life, operating with machine-like regularity.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: One day was very like another.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: At a certain time each morning the cooks turned out, fires were built, and breakfast was eaten.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Then, while some broke camp, others harnessed the dogs, and they were under way an hour or so before the darkness fell which gave warning of dawn.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: At night, camp was made.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Some pitched the flies, others cut firewood and pine boughs for the beds, and still others carried water or ice for the cooks.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Also, the dogs were fed.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: To them, this was the one feature of the day, though it was good to loaf around, after the fish was eaten, for an hour or so with the other dogs, of which there were fivescore and odd.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: There were fierce fighters among them, but three battles with the fiercest brought Buck to mastery, so that when he bristled and showed his teeth they got out of his way.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Best of all, perhaps, he loved to lie near the fire, hind legs crouched under him, fore legs stretched out in front, head raised, and eyes blinking dreamily at the flames.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Sometimes he thought of Judge Miller’s big house in the sun-kissed Santa Clara Valley, and of the cement swimming-tank, and Ysabel, the Mexican hairless, and Toots, the Japanese pug; but oftener he remembered the man in the red sweater, the death of Curly, the great fight with Spitz, and the good things he had eaten or would like to eat.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: He was not homesick.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: The Sunland was very dim and distant, and such memories had no power over him.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Far more potent were the memories of his heredity that gave things he had never seen before a seeming familiarity; the instincts (which were but the memories of his ancestors become habits) which had lapsed in later days, and still later, in him, quickened and become alive again.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Sometimes as he crouched there, blinking dreamily at the flames, it seemed that the flames were of another fire, and that as he crouched by this other fire he saw another and different man from the half-breed cook before him.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: This other man was shorter of leg and longer of arm, with muscles that were stringy and knotty rather than rounded and swelling.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: The hair of this man was long and matted, and his head slanted back under it from the eyes.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: He uttered strange sounds, and seemed very much afraid of the darkness, into which he peered continually, clutching in his hand, which hung midway between knee and foot, a stick with a heavy stone made fast to the end.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: He was all but naked, a ragged and fire-scorched skin hanging part way down his back, but on his body there was much hair.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: In some places, across the chest and shoulders and down the outside of the arms and thighs, it was matted into almost a thick fur.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: He did not stand erect, but with trunk inclined forward from the hips, on legs that bent at the knees.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: About his body there was a peculiar springiness, or resiliency, almost catlike, and a quick alertness as of one who lived in perpetual fear of things seen and unseen.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: At other times this hairy man squatted by the fire with head between his legs and slept.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: On such occasions his elbows were on his knees, his hands clasped above his head as though to shed rain by the hairy arms.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: And beyond that fire, in the circling darkness, Buck could see many gleaming coals, two by two, always two by two, which he knew to be the eyes of great beasts of prey.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: And he could hear the crashing of their bodies through the undergrowth, and the noises they made in the night.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: And dreaming there by the Yukon bank, with lazy eyes blinking at the fire, these sounds and sights of another world would make the hair to rise along his back and stand on end across his shoulders and up his neck, till he whimpered low and suppressedly, or growled softly, and the half-breed cook shouted at him, “Hey, you Buck, wake up!”

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Whereupon the other world would vanish and the real world come into his eyes, and he would get up and yawn and stretch as though he had been asleep.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: It was a hard trip, with the mail behind them, and the heavy work wore them down.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: They were short of weight and in poor condition when they made Dawson, and should have had a ten days’ or a week’s rest at least.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: But in two days’ time they dropped down the Yukon bank from the Barracks, loaded with letters for the outside.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: The dogs were tired, the drivers grumbling, and to make matters worse, it snowed every day.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: This meant a soft trail, greater friction on the runners, and heavier pulling for the dogs; yet the drivers were fair through it all, and did their best for the animals.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Each night the dogs were attended to first.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: They ate before the drivers ate, and no man sought his sleeping-robe till he had seen to the feet of the dogs he drove.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Still, their strength went down.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Since the beginning of the winter they had travelled eighteen hundred miles, dragging sleds the whole weary distance; and eighteen hundred miles will tell upon life of the toughest.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Buck stood it, keeping his mates up to their work and maintaining discipline, though he, too, was very tired.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Billee cried and whimpered regularly in his sleep each night.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Joe was sourer than ever, and Sol-leks was unapproachable, blind side or other side.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: But it was Dave who suffered most of all.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Something had gone wrong with him.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: He became more morose and irritable, and when camp was pitched at once made his nest, where his driver fed him.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Once out of the harness and down, he did not get on his feet again till harness-up time in the morning.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Sometimes, in the traces, when jerked by a sudden stoppage of the sled, or by straining to start it, he would cry out with pain.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: The driver examined him, but could find nothing.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: All the drivers became interested in his case.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: They talked it over at meal-time, and over their last pipes before going to bed, and one night they held a consultation.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: He was brought from his nest to the fire and was pressed and prodded till he cried out many times.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Something was wrong inside, but they could locate no broken bones, could not make it out.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: By the time Cassiar Bar was reached, he was so weak that he was falling repeatedly in the traces.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: The Scotch half-breed called a halt and took him out of the team, making the next dog, Sol-leks, fast to the sled.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: His intention was to rest Dave, letting him run free behind the sled.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter IV. Who Has Won to Mastership
saetze.text: Sick as he was, Dave resented being taken out, grunting and growling while the traces were unfastened, and whimpering broken-heartedly when he saw Sol-leks in the position he had held and served so long.

saetze.text: The Yeehats were dancing about the wreckage of the spruce-bough lodge when they heard a fearful roaring and saw rushing upon them an animal the like of which they had never seen before.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: It was Buck, a live hurricane of fury, hurling himself upon them in a frenzy to destroy.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: He sprang at the foremost man (it was the chief of the Yeehats), ripping the throat wide open till the rent jugular spouted a fountain of blood.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: He did not pause to worry the victim, but ripped in passing, with the next bound tearing wide the throat of a second man.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: There was no withstanding him.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: He plunged about in their very midst, tearing, rending, destroying, in constant and terrific motion which defied the arrows they discharged at him.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: In fact, so inconceivably rapid were his movements, and so closely were the Indians tangled together, that they shot one another with the arrows; and one young hunter, hurling a spear at Buck in mid air, drove it through the chest of another hunter with such force that the point broke through the skin of the back and stood out beyond.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: Then a panic seized the Yeehats, and they fled in terror to the woods, proclaiming as they fled the advent of the Evil Spirit.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: And truly Buck was the Fiend incarnate, raging at their heels and dragging them down like deer as they raced through the trees.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: It was a fateful day for the Yeehats.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: They scattered far and wide over the country, and it was not till a week later that the last of the survivors gathered together in a lower valley and counted their losses.

saetze.text: As for Buck, wearying of the pursuit, he returned to the desolated camp.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: By the edge, head and fore feet in the water, lay Skeet, faithful to the last.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: The pool itself, muddy and discolored from the sluice boxes, effectually hid what it contained, and it contained John Thornton; for Buck followed his trace into the water, from which no trace led away.

Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: All day Buck brooded by the pool or roamed restlessly about the camp.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: Death, as a cessation of movement, as a passing out and away from the lives of the living, he knew, and he knew John Thornton was dead.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: It left a great void in him, somewhat akin to hunger, but a void which ached and ached, and which food could not fill.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: At times, when he paused to contemplate the carcasses of the Yeehats, he forgot the pain of it; and at such times he was aware of a great pride in himself,—a pride greater than any he had yet experienced.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: He had killed man, the noblest game of all, and he had killed in the face of the law of club and fang.

saetze.text: He sniffed the bodies curiously.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: They had died so easily.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: It was harder to kill a husky dog than them.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: They were no match at all, were it not for their arrows and spears and clubs.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: Thenceforward he would be unafraid of them except when they bore in their hands their arrows, spears, and clubs.

Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: Night came on, and a full moon rose high over the trees into the sky, lighting the land till it lay bathed in ghostly day.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: And with the coming of the night, brooding and mourning by the pool, Buck became alive to a stirring of the new life in the forest other than that which the Yeehats had made.

saetze.text: He stood up, listening and scenting.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: From far away drifted a faint, sharp yelp, followed by a chorus of similar sharp yelps.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: As the moments passed the yelps grew closer and louder.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: Again Buck knew them as things heard in that other world which persisted in his memory.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: He walked to the centre of the open space and listened.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: It was the call, the many-noted call, sounding more luringly and compellingly than ever before.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: And as never before, he was ready to obey.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: John Thornton was dead.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: The last tie was broken.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: Man and the claims of man no longer bound him.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: Hunting their living meat, as the Yeehats were hunting it, on the flanks of the migrating moose, the wolf pack had at last crossed over from the land of streams and timber and invaded Buck’s valley.

saetze.text: Into the clearing where the moonlight streamed, they poured in a silvery flood; and in the centre of the clearing stood Buck, motionless as a statue, waiting their coming.

saetze.text: They were awed, so still and large he stood, and a moment’s pause fell, till the boldest one leaped straight for him.

saetze.kapitel: Chapter VII. The Sounding of the Call
saetze.text: They are afraid of this Ghost Dog, for it has cunning greater than they, stealing from their camps in fierce winters, robbing their traps, slaying their dogs, and defying their bravest hunters.
